verdict: Expedia grew revenue 12% to $4.9B as the travel it sells to other businesses surged 23%, turning its biggest quarter of the year into $1.0B of profit for shareholders.

segments.name: Lodging
segments.note: Hotel and vacation-rental bookings — the core of the business, up 11% as room nights rose 7%.

segments.name: Other travel
segments.note: Insurance, car rental, destination services and cruises — up 28%.

segments.name: Advertising — Expedia brands
segments.note: Ads sold on Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo — up 7%.

segments.name: Advertising — trivago
segments.note: Revenue from trivago, the hotel search site — up 20%.

segments.name: Air
segments.note: Plane tickets sold through the platform — down 7%.

opex.name: Selling & marketing — direct
opex.note: What it pays partners and search engines to bring in bookings.

opex.name: Technology & content
opex.note: Building and running the booking platform and its listings.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wearing-out cost of buildings, equipment and software.

opex.name: Selling & marketing — indirect
opex.note: Brand advertising and the marketing team's own costs.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal, HR and offices.

opex.name: Restructuring charges
opex.note: Costs of reorganizing the company — see one-time items.

opex.name: Legal reserves & occupancy tax
opex.note: Money set aside for legal and hotel-tax matters.

otherDetail: Interest income of $73M, less $63M of interest expense and $33M of other losses, net.

takeaways.title: Business travel is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Revenue from selling travel to other businesses (B2B) rose 23% to $1.7B, while the consumer brands grew 6%. Partners, not just travelers, are driving Expedia now.

takeaways.title: More of each dollar stuck
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA — a rough measure of operating cash profit — was $1.69B, or 34.2 cents per revenue dollar, up from 32.9 cents a year ago.

takeaways.title: Profit rose even after a bigger tax bill
takeaways.text: Net income was $1,039M in total; $1,030M belonged to Expedia shareholders ($9M to minority partners). The tax provision rose to $264M from $167M a year ago.

oneTimers: $35M of restructuring and reorganization charges in the quarter ($104M so far in 2026).
Seasonal cash pattern: operating cash flow was negative $1,157M in Q3 as traveler deposits collected earlier in the year were paid out to hotels — normal for Expedia's peak season, not a loss.
footerNote: Net income of $1,039M is the total before $9M allocated to non-controlling interests; $1,030M was attributable to Expedia Group shareholders.
